title: Jump straight to a record
description:
Text files must be read from the start. A **binary** file of fixed-size records can be read at any position, because record number `n` begins at byte `n × sizeof(Record)`.

Using the `Record` struct provided (it is plain data, so its bytes can be written directly), write:

- `bool writeRecords(const std::filesystem::path& file, const std::vector<Record>& records)`: writes them one after another in binary mode.
- `std::optional<Record> readRecord(const std::filesystem::path& file, std::size_t index)`: seeks to that record and reads only it. Returns `std::nullopt` if the file is missing or has no such record.
- `std::size_t recordCount(const std::filesystem::path& file)`: from the file's size.

Open with `std::ios::binary`. Write with `out.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(&record), sizeof(Record))` and read with the matching `in.read(...)`. `in.seekg(position)` moves the read position.
hints: Open with `std::ios::binary` and write each record with `out.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(&r), sizeof r);`.
To read one, `in.seekg(index * sizeof(Record));` then `in.read(...)` into a `Record`; if the read did not get a whole record (`in.gcount() != sizeof(Record)`), return `std::nullopt`.
